brief: US equity dispersion resumed this week: AI/Tech (Meta Muse agentic adoption, Micron pre-EPS upside buying) rallied while Energy/Financials/Utilities sold off, pushing single-stock moves to a 95th-percentile spread versus the unchanged index over the past month. Low correlation keeps index vol low, reinforced by massive 0/1 DTE gamma supply from VRP/QIS flows (selling daily 25-delta SPX puts scores 6 Sharpe over 1 month, 3 Sharpe over 3 months). Outside equities, fixed-income/macro vol has woken up, with PnL losses and pod stop-outs from crowded Carry (and Trend) positioning unwinding on a realized-vol reset. Pain points: EUR swaptions squeezed, the 3rd-largest 2-day move in USD 1m10y this decade, OAT-STR spreads crunched, curves flattening the wrong way, MXN carry unwinding, credit leaking, EM sovereign credit (Argentina, Venezuela, Ukraine, Ecuador) sharply off highs. Some investors hope for reversal via month/quarter-end pension UST rebalancing, but bonds keep failing to hold rallies. The long end is leading today's slip despite lower oil and higher equities. McElligott argues the next acute rate shock (hot data or a US diesel export ban) would reprice markets for a growth shock, and recommends long-dated swaption straddles for cheap long-vega exposure.
